pairs.subject: rate-limiting
pairs.evidence: src/lib/rate-limit.ts:35 On the default self-hosted posture (no ASCENT_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS and no VERCEL witness), every anonymous caller of every per-IP door lands in one shared 'unknown' burst bucket with no spread layer, so ordinary traffic exhausts one caller's allowance together. Separately, every refusal does a fire-and-forget DB upsert, which puts a remote, per-request-billed write on the refusal hot path.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/public-scan-quota.ts:200 Both limiters are sliding-window logs and record only admitted hits. A denied monthly decision returns the trimmed window without `now`, and the burst window does the same (QUOTA #2 in rate-limit-window.ts checkWindow). The 30-day budget is durable (Prisma) because the in-memory window would reset on restart. Minor gap: elapsed-time math uses Date.now() (wall clock), not a monotonic source.

src/lib/public-scan-quota.ts:148 bucketContext is the single derivation for consume, peek and refund. Signed-in callers get a per-user key in a separate namespace. The horizon rule is realized: the monthly gate treats the 'unknown' sentinel as unenforceable (fail open), while the burst limiter pools it. MCP is keyed on the verified token id. The in-memory map has a reaper that evicts only fully-aged keys, but no hard size cap.

src/lib/rate-limit.ts:69 Every config must declare a basis. Each entry has a cost justification, a CLEARS cadence check and an honest 'NOT DERIVED' label, and is env-overridable. There is one budget per operation class. The monthly quota is labelled a friction nudge, not a security control (public-scan-quota.ts:17).

src/lib/public-scan-quota.ts:341 The /api/quota peek reads without consuming and uses the same windowState arithmetic as decideQuota, so the meter and the refusal speak one truth. QuotaMeter shows standing (with a low-allowance warn state) before the first refusal. Refusal series are named by limiter and layer, and rateLimiterStats exposes reaper metrics. Gaps: no admitted/demand series, and no limit-change event record.

src/lib/rate-limit.ts:1 The mechanics are right: one charge pipeline reserves, then commits or releases across layers (QUOTA #1/#3); a shared store fails closed in front of spend; fail-open is an opt-in bound. But the door list is stale. The header names 3 doors, while the limiter now covers gate, mcp, quota, peek, contact, org-repos, branding and ingest. The scan route comment says 'these two are the only routes on the shared scan budget', yet gate/[owner]/[repo]/route.ts:104 also charges SCAN_RATE_LIMIT. The doors are therefore not enumerated.

src/lib/public-scan-quota.ts:364 The monthly quota charges the costly step (an LLM-backed scan that actually delivered) and refunds the exact charged slot when nothing chargeable was produced. Cache-hit hydration and peek are kept off the scan budget.

src/lib/rate-limit.ts:93 A refusal names its layer, limiter, limit and window (per-IP only; the global ceiling is withheld on purpose). retry-after is computed from the oldest in-window hit. The could-not-evaluate path is spelled distinctly (rate_limit_unavailable, evaluated:false, breaker-derived retry). Standard 429 + Retry-After are used. Minor: the verdict is a boolean plus optional fields, not a closed union.

src/lib/db/quota-events.ts:41 countRefusal in rate-limit-charge.ts calls recordQuotaEvent on every refusal, which is a DB upsert on one hot (kind, scope) row per rejection. That is a remote, per-request-billed write (the repo notes Aurora DSQL bills per request) on the refusal path at storm rate, instead of an in-process counter flushed periodically. The reaper itself is conformant: cadenced, bounded, observable.

src/lib/rate-limit.ts:35 Unattributable callers are pooled into one 'unknown' bucket by default (hops=0 is the unwitnessed default), with no coarse fingerprint spread. A global ceiling exists above it, but only half the spread-then-cap pair ships. The MCP comment (rate-limit.ts:392-394) admits this made every agent share one 60/min budget.

src/lib/rate-limit.ts:37 Earlier finding resolved: hops now defaults to 0 unless the VERCEL witness is present, the operator opt-in carries a depth, and chains are read from the right. Negative tests exist (rate-limit.test.ts:177). Still missing: the accepted header text becomes a map key after only a trim, with no IP parse, single canonical form or length cap. The rung is not returned with the value. And hops=1 on an operator opt-in also trusts x-real-ip, which the declared proxy may not overwrite.

pairs.registryProposal: key-design ('pool and refuse at burst horizons') and unattributable-client-bucketing ('never pool by default') give opposite defaults for a burst-window limiter whose default deployment makes ALL traffic unattributable. The standard could state outright that the key-design pooling allowance holds only when unattributable traffic is a small minority.
